newsitem.title: UK: PNG metals sector seen little affected after crisis.
newsitem.headline: PNG metals sector seen little affected after crisis.

text.p: Scant immediate impact was expected in Papua New Guinea's output of copper and other metals after the decision on Wednesday by the prime minister to step down after widespread protests.
Fighting on the island of Bougainville, which helped spark the crisis, was no closer to a solution, so the huge Panguna copper and gold mine would stay shut for the immediate future, analysts said.
Production at Ok Tedi and other existing mines would unlikely to be affected.
"At the moment I think it's too early to say if there will be any changes whatsoever," said analyst Jim Lennon at broker Macquarie Equities.

Prime Minister Sir Julius Chan told parliament a caretaker administration would take over after 10 days of popular and military protests over his decision to pay $36 million to foreign mercenaries to crush a secessionist war in Bougainville.
"What can the army do that they haven't already tried to do over the past eight years?" Lennon asked.
Rebels in May 1989 shut the giant Panguna mine operated by Bougainville Copper Ltd.
"All we can do is watch and wait," said John Hughes, head of public affairs in London for RTZ Corp Plc-CRA Ltd, which owns 53.6 percent of Bougainville Copper.
The firm said on Sunday it had not given up on the mine as a lost cause.
"No, it's not -- it's still a very, very important asset...and we still intend to go back there," RTZ-CRA Chief Executive Leon Davis said on Australian television.

But even if the government and rebels agreed to a political solution, re-opening the mine would cost up to $434 million and take about 18 months, Bougainville Chairman David Karpin said in the firm's 1996 annual report.
During the mine's 17 years of operation, it produced concentrate containing three million tonnes of copper, 306 tonnes of gold and 784 tonnes of silver.
Recoverable ore reserves at the end of 1995 were 496 million tonnes of average grade 0.42 percent copper and 0.55 grames per tonne of gold.
RTZ's Davis has also said that it remained committed to its investment in the Lihir gold project in the country.
Gold production from Lihir Gold Ltd's oxide ore is on schedule to begin production in May of 175,000 ounces in 1997, with output of 550,000 ounces in 1998.
Activity at the Ok Tedi mine, which produces 600,000 tonnes of copper concentrate annually, should not be affected by the political changes in the capital Port Moresby, analysts said.

"The OK Tedi mine is remote from the politics sweeping the country and on balance looks unlikely to be affected for the moment," said analyst Larry Kaplan of Flemings Global Mining Group in a commentary.
The mine's operator, Broken Hill Proprietary Co Ltd, said on Monday that shipments by barge down a river had resumed after being halted due to drought.
